## https://udyoggrowth.com/solar-subsidy-pm-surya-ghar/
PM Surya Ghar Solar Subsidy — ₹78,000 Claim | Udyog Growth Udyog Growth ☰ Subsidies & Finance PMFME & MoFPI Subsidy MSME Schemes Business Loans & Subsidy CMA Data & Bankable DPR GST, Tenders & Trade Regulatory Affairs Labour Code / EPF / ESIC BIS Certification ISO Certification PESO License Industrial Approvals Advance Authorisation / EPCG GeM Suspension / Disputes CMA Data / DPR GST Notices & Litigation GeM & Tenders Import-Export (IEC/DGFT) Advance Authorisation & EPCG GeM Suspension & Disputes Licensing & Approvals FSSAI Food License Liquor & Excise (Delhi) Land Conversion / CLU Solar Subsidy Pollution NOC PESO License Industrial Approvals & SEZ Labour & Certification Labour Code, EPF & ESIC BIS Certification (ISI/CRS) ISO Certification NGO & Schools NGO / Trust / CSR School Affiliation (CBSE/CISCE) Delhi Nursery Admissions Delhi Top Schools List Regulatory Affairs Cities Delhi & New Delhi Noida & Greater Noida Gurugram Faridabad Ghaziabad Patna Bihar (all districts) BIADA & Bihar incentives Tools All services Call Home / Solar Subsidy (PM Surya Ghar) PM Surya Ghar Solar Subsidy — Claim, Net Metering & Rejection-Proofing (Delhi-NCR) Quick answer: Residential subsidy under PM Surya Ghar: ₹30,000 per kW up to 2 kW , plus ₹18,000 for the 3rd kW — capped at ₹78,000 for 3 kW and above (₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW). Paid by DBT, typically 30–45 days after DISCOM commissioning. Apply on pmsuryaghar.gov.in; equipment must be ALMM-listed ; group housing societies get ₹18,000/kW for common facilities up to 500 kW. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. The #1 reason subsidy claims get rejected: a panel or inverter that isn't on the MNRE ALMM list — followed by the electricity-connection name not matching the applicant. Both are checked after you've spent the money, so we verify vendor, equipment and paperwork before installation, not at claim stage. What you actually get System size Subsidy 1 kW ₹30,000 2 kW ₹60,000 3 kW and above ₹78,000 (cap) Group housing society / RWA (common facilities) ₹18,000 per kW, up to 500 kW (max 3 kW per house) Eligibility: a residential electricity connection with sanctioned load up to 10 kW, the application in the same name as the electricity bill, and no earlier rooftop-solar subsidy on the connection. We check your eligibility and vendor's equipment against this list before installation starts — catching a disqualifying issue after the panels are up is far more expensive than catching it before. The claim sequence — where files get stuck Portal registration on pmsuryaghar.gov.in with DISCOM and consumer number. Feasibility approval from the DISCOM — sanctioned-load and technical checks happen here. Installation by a registered vendor with ALMM-listed panels and inverter — the step where a wrong equipment choice silently kills the subsidy. Net metering + commissioning — meter installation and DISCOM inspection. DBT disbursal — bank details on the portal; money typically lands 30–45 days after commissioning. We chase every stage so the file never idles. Commercial & industrial rooftops — a different game PM Surya Ghar is residential; shops, offices and factories don't get this subsidy. Commercial rooftop works on economics instead: net-metering/net-billing arrangements with your DISCOM, capex-vs-PPA structuring (third-party investor owns the plant, you buy power cheaper), and the accounting treatment of the asset. We structure the DISCOM approvals and the PPA so the project stands on savings, not on a subsidy that doesn't exist for you. Factory or commercial installation as part of a bigger setup? Solar sits alongside pollution consents and the project-finance file — we handle the full approval stack. Who this is for Homeowners across Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Ghaziabad, Gurugram and Faridabad claiming the subsidy correctly the first time; RWAs and group housing societies for common-area systems; applicants whose claim is stuck or was rejected; and businesses evaluating commercial rooftop with net metering or a PPA. Want the subsidy without the rejection cycle? Call for a free consultation Our methodology: precision, persistence, presence Procedural mastery — we prepare every file to meet the specific technical criteria of the relevant department, minimising queries and delays. Dedicated coordination — consistent follow-up on your application so it keeps moving through the standard workflow. Compliance-first documentation — built to withstand scrutiny, protecting your business from future audits or objections. Frequently Asked Questions How much subsidy do I get under PM Surya Ghar? Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW, plus Rs 18,000 for the 3rd kW — capped at Rs 78,000 for systems of 3 kW or more. So 1 kW gets Rs 30,000, 2 kW gets Rs 60,000, and 3 kW or larger gets Rs 78,000, paid by DBT to your bank account after DISCOM commissioning. Who is eligible for the PM Surya Ghar subsidy? A residential consumer with sanctioned load up to 10 kW, applying in the same name as on the electricity bill, with no earlier rooftop-solar subsidy on that connection. Group housing societies and RWAs are separately eligible at Rs 18,000/kW for common facilities up to 500 kW (max 3 kW per house). Why do PM Surya Ghar subsidy claims get rejected? The most common cause is equipment — a panel or inverter not on the MNRE ALMM list — followed by the applicant's name not matching the electricity connection, and missing roof-ownership proof. All three are preventable before installation; almost none are fixable after. We verify the vendor's equipment list against ALMM before you sign. How long does the subsidy take to arrive? Typically 30–45 days after the DISCOM commissions the plant and your bank details are verified on the portal. Delays usually trace to pending DISCOM inspection or a bank-detail mismatch — both chase-able, which is exactly what we do. Can my shop, office or factory get the PM Surya Ghar subsidy? No — the scheme is for residential connections. Commercial and industrial rooftops work on net-metering/net-billing economics and PPA structuring instead, which often beats a subsidy anyway at commercial tariffs. We structure the DISCOM approvals and the PPA for exactly this. Is there a loan available for rooftop solar under the scheme? Banks run dedicated PM Surya Ghar loan products for residential systems with simplified processing. Whether a loan makes sense depends on your tariff and consumption; we run the payback math with and without financing before you commit. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Are the FSSAI turnover limits really ₹1.5 crore and ₹50 crore now? Yes. The FSSAI Order of 13 March 2026, effective 1 April 2026, raised Basic Registration to turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, State Licence to ₹1.5–50 crore, and Central Licence above ₹50 crore. Many guides still show the old ₹12 lakh / ₹20 crore slabs. Is DIR-3 KYC really once in three years now? Yes. Under G.S.R. 943(E), effective 31 March 2026, directors file DIR-3 KYC once in every three consecutive financial years by 30 June, using the single DIR-3 KYC Web form. A change of mobile, email or address must still be updated within 30 days. Why does the Shop Act result differ between Delhi and Noida? Uttar Pradesh and Haryana amended their Shops & Establishments Acts in 2025 to require registration only at 20 or more employees. Delhi's matching 2026 amendment has been published but not yet brought into force, so Delhi still requires registration at any headcount. Can I rely on these results to file? Use them to understand where you stand, then let us verify against your documents and the live portal before filing — thresholds and forms change, and some kinds of business have activity-based rules that override turnover. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Central jurisdiction is the CGST Gurugram Commissionerate (Haryana Zone); State jurisdiction is the Haryana Excise & Taxation Department's Gurugram circles. Which one issued your notice decides where we appear — we check the GSTIN jurisdiction before drafting a single line. We have a Gurugram unit and a Delhi head office — do we need two replies to one notice? Each GSTIN is a separate registration with its own jurisdictional officer, so a Haryana notice is answered in Haryana even if your books sit in Delhi. We handle both from one file so the facts and figures stay consistent across states. Udyog Vihar and Manesar factories often get ITC-mismatch notices — why? Job-work movements, inter-unit stock transfers and large vendor bases create GSTR-2B gaps that look like excess ITC. Most are timing or classification differences, not genuine excess claims; the reply has to prove that invoice by invoice. Does GST 2.0 change anything for Gurugram service exporters in Cyber City? Rates changed for goods more than services, but LUT discipline, place-of-supply rules and refund timelines are where Cyber City IT/ITES exporters actually get stuck — we keep the LUT current every April and track refund RFD-01 filings. Can you appear at the Gurugram office physically? Yes. What is the deadline to reply to a DRC-01 in Gurugram? The same as everywhere in India — 30 days from service (DRC-01C intimations are 7 days; ASMT-10 scrutiny notices usually 30). Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which authority issues FSSAI licences in Noida? Basic Registrations and State Licences come from the Food Safety & Drug Administration (FSDA), Uttar Pradesh — Designated Officer, Gautam Buddh Nagar. Central Licences are issued by FSSAI's regional office; the inspection is still done locally. What are the FSSAI turnover limits in 2026? From 1 April 2026: Basic Registration for turnover up to ₹1.5 crore, State Licence from ₹1.5 crore to ₹50 crore, Central Licence above ₹50 crore (FSSAI Order of 13 March 2026). Many guides still show the old ₹12 lakh / ₹20 crore slabs. Do FSSAI licences still need renewal? No. Licences issued under the Licensing and Registration Amendment Regulations, 2026 do not expire; an annual fee keeps them active. Existing licences move to the new regime on renewal. How long does FSSAI take here? Basic Registration is usually issued within 7 working days of a complete application; State and Central Licences depend on the Designated Officer's inspection scheduling, typically 30 working days per the portal SLA — we track the file through inspection rather than waiting on it. What does it cost? Government fees: Basic ₹100 per year; State ₹2,000 per year for most businesses (₹5,000 for large manufacturers and 4-star-plus hotels); Central ₹7,500 per year. Our professional fee is quoted after a short call, before any work begins. Can you handle the inspection in Noida if I'm not local? Yes — we coordinate the Designated Officer's visit, prepare the premises checklist (layout, water test, pest control, medical fitness certificates) and attend where the department permits. © 2026 Udyog Growth. What we handle in Ghaziabad Matter Where it is heard Our role DRC-01 / show-cause notices CGST Ghaziabad or UP State Tax Ghaziabad zone (by GSTIN jurisdiction) Point-by-point DRC-06 reply, personal hearing E-way bill detention (MOV-07 / MOV-09, s.129) Mobile squad / jurisdictional officer Transport-record reply, release of goods, penalty contest ASMT-10 scrutiny & DRC-01C ITC mismatch Jurisdictional officer Invoice-level 2B reconciliation, ASMT-11 / Part B reply Departmental audit & assessment Audit Commissionerate / State audit wing Document preparation, representation through closure Appeals Appellate Authority; GSTAT Uttar Pradesh bench APL-01 with 10% pre-deposit, tribunal filing Registration, APOB, LUT, refunds Portal / jurisdictional officer Rule 14A fast-track registration, additional place of business, annual LUT, RFD-01 We serve businesses across Ghaziabad's industrial and trading belts — Sahibabad Industrial Area (Site 4), Meerut Road and Bulandshahr Road industrial areas, Kavi Nagar Industrial Area, Mohan Nagar and Loni manufacturing clusters, and the commercial corridors of Indirapuram, Vaishali, Raj Nagar Extension and Kaushambi. Being the first UP district across the Delhi border, Ghaziabad runs more interstate e-way bill, warehouse-GSTIN and place-of-supply questions than almost anywhere else in NCR. Uttar Pradesh-specific: no Professional Tax; Shop & Establishment registration applies at 20+ employees under the UP Amendment Act 2025; pollution consent runs through UPPCB; industrial approvals route via Nivesh Mitra 3.0; the trade licence comes from Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam. A GST notice is rarely the only thing a Ghaziabad unit has open — we check the rest while we're at it. Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Client: A Sahibabad packaging manufacturer dispatching daily to Delhi, approximately 45 employees. Situation: Goods detained on the Delhi border under section 129 for an expired e-way bill; MOV-07 notice with penalty equal to 200% of tax proposed. Approach: Produced the transporter's breakdown record and toll data to show the expiry arose in transit without intent, filed the MOV-09 reply within the window, and secured release against bond while contesting the penalty. Outcome: Goods released; penalty reduced to the procedural-lapse level on adjudication. Client identity and certain details have been changed or withheld to protect confidentiality. Outcomes depend on individual facts and are not a guarantee of results. Related: our main GST notice-defence page , the Noida and Delhi practices, and UP Shop Act, EPF & ESIC compliance . Manufacturing here? Pollution NOC (CTE/CTO) for this board . New registration? The 3-working-day Rule 14A route applies here too. Detained at the border? E-way bill detention — section 129 reply, release and appeal . Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which GST office handles Ghaziabad businesses? Central jurisdiction is the CGST Ghaziabad Commissionerate; State jurisdiction is the Uttar Pradesh State Tax (Commercial Tax) Department's Ghaziabad zone. The notice itself tells you which — we confirm the GSTIN's assigned jurisdiction before drafting. Sahibabad and Meerut Road units get a lot of e-way bill notices — why? High-frequency dispatches to Delhi across the border create e-way bill expiry, vehicle-mismatch and Part-B errors that trigger MOV-07/MOV-09 proceedings under section 129. Most are procedural lapses, not evasion, and the reply has to show that with transport records. Do UP rules differ from Delhi for a Ghaziabad business? For GST itself, no — one Act, but a separate State officer. Around it, yes: UP's Shop Act now applies at 20+ employees (not at any size, as in Delhi), there is no Professional Tax, pollution consent runs through UPPCB, and approvals route via Nivesh Mitra 3.0. Can a Delhi-registered business with a Ghaziabad godown ignore UP registration? No — a place of business in UP from which supplies are made needs a UP GSTIN. Operating a Ghaziabad warehouse on a Delhi GSTIN alone is a common trigger for a REG-17 or section 122 notice. Will you appear in person at the Ghaziabad office? Yes — hearings, document verification and follow-up at CGST Ghaziabad and the UP State Tax office are part of the engagement. What is the reply deadline for a DRC-01 in Ghaziabad? 30 days from service, as everywhere in India; DRC-01C intimations are 7 days and ASMT-10 scrutiny notices usually 30. The local office does not change the statutory clock. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which ROC handles a company registered in Noida? The Registrar of Companies, Uttar Pradesh (Kanpur). Incorporation itself is filed centrally through MCA's SPICe+, but the ROC's jurisdiction decides where later filings, inspections and show-cause matters are heard. Does Uttar Pradesh charge different stamp duty on incorporation? Yes — stamp duty on the MOA, AOA and share certificates is a state levy and differs between UP, Haryana and Bihar. SPICe+ computes it automatically from the registered-office state; we make sure the registered office you declare is the one you actually operate from, since changing it later across states is a Regional Director matter. How long does company registration take? Name approval and SPICe+ filing are portal-driven; a complete, correctly-documented application is typically approved within the MCA's standard processing window (around 7 working days as per portal SLA). Delays almost always come from name conflicts, document defects or DSC issues — all avoidable. What do I get at incorporation? Certificate of Incorporation with CIN, PAN and TAN, EPFO and ESIC registrations, and a bank-account opening request — all through the single SPICe+ (AGILE-PRO) filing. GST can be included in the same filing or taken separately once the registered office is ready. Which structure should I choose? Private Limited if you plan to raise investment, issue ESOPs or have foreign shareholders; LLP for professional and service firms wanting limited liability with lighter compliance; OPC for a solo founder wanting company status. Try our free structure quiz , then call. What compliance follows incorporation? INC-20A within 180 days, auditor appointment (ADT-1), annual ROC filing (AOC-4, MGT-7/7A), and DIR-3 KYC for every director — now once in three years under the rule effective 31 March 2026. Under the revised small-company limits (₹10 crore capital / ₹100 crore turnover), most new companies get the lighter tier. © 2026 Udyog Growth. The three thresholds every Noida employer gets wrong Registration Applies at Authority / portal Note Shop & Establishment (Uttar Pradesh) 20+ employees UP Labour Department via Nivesh Mitra 3.0 No registration required below 20 ESIC 10+ employees (employer-level count) ESIC portal Wage ceiling ₹21,000/month; register each employee within 10 days of joining EPF 20+ employees EPFO Unified Portal Wage ceiling ₹15,000 for mandatory coverage; ECR by the 15th Factory licence (manufacturers) 20+ workers with power / 40+ without Uttar Pradesh Labour Dept under the OSH Code Separate from Shop Act; plan approval is a physical step Uttar Pradesh rule, current as of 4 October 2026: Under the UP Amendment Act 2025 (effective November 2025), registration is mandatory only for establishments with 20 or more employees , within six months of starting. Below 20, no Shop Act registration is required. The amendment also widened 'commercial establishment' to cover medical practitioners, architects and delivery services — so clinics and app-based delivery hubs in Noida are now squarely inside the Act once they cross 20. Delhi is different — its matching amendment is published but not yet in force, so a Delhi office still registers at any headcount. If you have premises on both sides of the border, the two files are not the same file. We serve Sector 62–63 IT offices and BPOs, Sector 18 retail and restaurants, Expressway-sector startups, Greater Noida's Knowledge Park institutes and the Ecotech manufacturers that also need a factory licence. No Professional Tax is levied in Uttar Pradesh, so if a vendor is quoting you for PT registration here, that is a red flag about the rest of their advice. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Does my Noida office need a Shop & Establishment registration? Under the UP Amendment Act 2025 (effective November 2025), registration is mandatory only for establishments with 20 or more employees, within six months of starting. Below 20, no Shop Act registration is required. The amendment also widened 'commercial establishment' to cover medical practitioners, architects and delivery services — so clinics and app-based delivery hubs in Noida are now squarely inside the Act once they cross 20. Which portal handles it in Noida? UP Labour Department via Nivesh Mitra 3.0. We file it, track the acknowledgement and keep the registers the department can ask for on inspection. When does EPF apply? At 20 or more employees, nationally — mandatory for employees earning up to ₹15,000 per month, voluntary coverage above. Monthly ECR is due by the 15th. Under the Code on Wages, basic plus DA must be at least 50% of total pay, which raises the PF base for many employers. When does ESIC apply? At 10 or more employees (counted at employer level, not per branch), for employees earning up to ₹21,000 per month gross — ₹25,000 for persons with disability. The ₹30,000 ceiling you may have read about has not been notified. Do I still need a Shop Act certificate for a bank account or GST? Banks and GST accept other proofs (incorporation certificate, Udyam, rent agreement). If your establishment is below the state's registration threshold, a Shop Act certificate is not something you can or need to obtain — we provide the right alternative proof instead. What changed with the four Labour Codes? They came into force on 21 November 2025. For a Shop Act-type establishment the practical changes are the new wage definition, mandatory appointment letters, single registration under the OSH Code at 10+ workers, and the factory-licence threshold moving to 20+ workers with power. State rules are still being finalised; we check your state's current status before filing. © 2026 Udyog Growth. The two files that have to move together Step Portal / authority What it decides Stage-1 clearance (approval in principle) Single Window Clearance, swc2.bihar.gov.in — State Investment Promotion Board Incentive eligibility; 15-working-day standard for complete applications Land / shed allotment biada1.bihar.gov.in — BIADA allotment committee, under the Land Allotment & Management Policy (Revised) 2026 Plot or Plug & Play shed, lease terms, possession Consents that follow Bihar State Pollution Control Board; Labour Resources Dept (factory licence under the OSH Code); FSSAI/other sector licences Whether you can build and operate Incentive claim Department of Industries Capital subsidy / interest subvention / SGST reimbursement under the policy you applied under Status, verified 4 October 2026: the Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package 2025 — the one with ₹1 token land for very large projects and 50% land-rate concession for others — closed to new applications on 31 March 2026 . If you applied in time, the file is in processing and we can take it over. If you did not, the incentives you qualify for depend on the policy in force on the day you apply — do not build a projection on last year's package. We check the live position before you sign anything. Plug & Play shed rates — the published schedule For units that want to start without building, BIADA lets ready sheds on monthly rent. The rates published on BIADA's shed-details page (checked 4 October 2026) differ sharply by estate: Industrial area Published rent (per sq ft per month) Note IA Fatuha (Patna district, NH-30) ₹8 Food-processing and logistics cluster IA New Bihta / Sikandarpur ₹8 Growth belt with the state's first ICD; most available space IA Patliputra (Patna city) ₹25 Oldest estate, fully allotted plots; sheds rarely vacant IA Udyog Bhawan (East Gandhi Maidan, Patna) ₹60 City-centre; suits offices and light assembly Vacancy changes weekly — we check the live shed list before advising. BIADA's head office is at Udyog Bhawan, East Gandhi Maidan, Patna (helpline 7280004800); the Managing Director hears grievances every working Tuesday at 3 PM. A shed is also the fastest route to a Consent to Operate and a bank sanction while a plot application is in process. What actually gets applications rejected or stalled Applying for land before Stage-1 clearance — the two are sequenced, and the SWC file is what the incentive later hangs on A DPR whose investment and employment numbers don't match across the SWC form, the BIADA form and the bank — one inconsistent figure invites a query on all three Asking for more land than the project justifies; the committee tests area against investment and sector norms Ignoring possession-and-production timelines in the lease — BIADA cancels allotments that don't start Treating pollution consent as an afterthought; for most manufacturing it decides whether the plot is usable at all What we do Choose the estate and plot size that fit the project — Patliputra, Fatuha, Bihta, or elsewhere in the state Stage-1 clearance on SWC, then the BIADA online application with a DPR built to the committee's tests Lease execution, possession, and the possession-to-production calendar BSPCB consent , factory licence and EPF/ESIC , FSSAI and sector licences, sequenced The incentive claim itself — and PMFME or CGTMSE alongside, where the unit qualifies Representation at BIADA and the Department of Industries, including the Managing Director's weekly grievance hearing (every working Tuesday, 3 PM) Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions How do I apply for a BIADA plot? Online only, on biada1.bihar.gov.in, against the Land Bank (available plots) or the Plug & Play shed bank, under the BIADA Land Allotment & Management Policy (Revised), 2026. Applications are scrutinised on project viability, investment and sector priority and decided by the allotment committee; a lease agreement and possession follow. Is the 2025 Industrial Investment Promotion Package still open? The application window on the Single Window Clearance portal closed on 31 March 2026. Units that applied in time are being processed; new units are governed by whichever policy is in force on the date they apply — we confirm the current instrument before you commit to a plot or a projection. What did the 2025 package offer? For units applying by the deadline: land at a token ₹1 for investments above ₹100 crore with 1,000 direct jobs (up to 10 acres) or above ₹1,000 crore (up to 25 acres), 50% concession on BIADA land rates for other qualifying units, and one of three mutually exclusive incentive routes — interest subvention and SGST reimbursement, or capital subsidy — plus stamp-duty and land-conversion reimbursement. What is the Stage-1 clearance? Approval in principle from the State Investment Promotion Board through swc2.bihar.gov.in, with a 15-working-day service standard for complete applications. It is the gate for incentive eligibility and should be sequenced before, not after, the land application. Which BIADA estates are near Patna? Patliputra Industrial Area (the oldest, fully allotted), Fatuha on NH-30, and Bihta — the growth belt with the state's first inland container depot and the largest available land. Hajipur is across the river in Vaishali district and often grouped with Patna. Can you handle BIADA if I'm based in Delhi-NCR? Yes — a large share of BIADA applicants are NCR businesses setting up a Bihar unit for incentives or market access. We run the SWC and BIADA filings, the pollution consent, FSSAI/factory licence and the subsidy claim from Delhi, and appear in Patna when the file needs a person in the room, including the MD's weekly grievance hearing if it comes to that. © 2026 Udyog Growth. ## https://udyoggrowth.com/bihar-startup-policy-seed-fund/
Bihar Startup Policy — ₹10 Lakh Seed Fund | Udyog Growth Udyog Growth ☰ Subsidies & Finance PMFME & MoFPI Subsidy MSME Schemes Business Loans & Subsidy CMA Data & Bankable DPR GST, Tenders & Trade Regulatory Affairs Labour Code / EPF / ESIC BIS Certification ISO Certification PESO License Industrial Approvals Advance Authorisation / EPCG GeM Suspension / Disputes CMA Data / DPR GST Notices & Litigation GeM & Tenders Import-Export (IEC/DGFT) Advance Authorisation & EPCG GeM Suspension & Disputes Licensing & Approvals FSSAI Food License Liquor & Excise (Delhi) Land Conversion / CLU Solar Subsidy Pollution NOC PESO License Industrial Approvals & SEZ Labour & Certification Labour Code, EPF & ESIC BIS Certification (ISI/CRS) ISO Certification NGO & Schools NGO / Trust / CSR School Affiliation (CBSE/CISCE) Delhi Nursery Admissions Delhi Top Schools List Regulatory Affairs Cities Delhi & New Delhi Noida & Greater Noida Gurugram Faridabad Ghaziabad Patna Bihar (all districts) BIADA & Bihar incentives Tools All services Call Home / Bihar Startup Policy & Seed Fund Bihar Startup Policy — Recognition & the ₹10 Lakh Seed Fund Quick answer: The Bihar Startup Policy 2022-27 gives recognised startups a seed grant of up to ₹10 lakh as an interest-free, 10-year, non-dilutive loan released against milestones, plus a ₹3 lakh accelerator grant and free workspace. Recognition on startup.bihar.gov.in comes first; the application is judged as a business plan — we build it to the rating framework. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. What the policy offers, stage by stage Stage Support Form Recognition Certification as a Bihar startup by the Nodal Agency Application on startup.bihar.gov.in; gate for everything below Validation Seed grant up to ₹10 lakh (higher for women- and SC/ST-led) Interest-free loan, 10 years, milestone-linked, no equity Acceleration ₹3 lakh on completing an approved accelerator programme Grant Early revenue Post-seed support once revenue thresholds are crossed Per policy terms Scale-up Bihar Startup Scale-up Financing Fund (₹50 crore, SIDBI-managed) Through SEBI-registered AIFs, not direct Throughout Free co-working space, patent-filing support, 10% space reserved in new industrial parks, regulatory self-certification On recognition The honest version: the ₹10 lakh is a loan — interest-free and non-dilutive, which is excellent, but repayable. It is released in tranches against milestones after the Startup Support Unit rates the startup, so the application is really a business plan review, not a form. That is where most first attempts fall short. What we do Check the three eligibility gates up front: Bihar incorporation and office, age/turnover limits, and the innovation test the screening applies Entity setup if needed — company or LLP in Patna — with the Bihar office documented properly Startup Bihar recognition application and, in parallel, Startup India/DPIIT recognition on NSWS The seed-fund file: pitch, financials, milestones written to the rating framework, and the follow-up until disbursement The registrations a funded startup then needs — GST , Udyam, EPF/ESIC , trademark — sequenced so the first tranche isn't held up by a missing certificate Food, agri or manufacturing startup? We pair this with PMFME and BIADA where they fit Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Client: Two Patna graduates with an agri-logistics app, pre-revenue. Situation: First seed-fund application returned — strong idea, but the financials showed no milestones and the Bihar office was a home address with no evidence of operations. Approach: Registered the LLP with a documented co-working office, rebuilt the plan around six measurable milestones mapped to tranches, filed DPIIT recognition alongside, and resubmitted. Outcome: Recognised; seed fund sanctioned with the first tranche released against milestone one. Client identity and certain details have been changed or withheld to protect confidentiality. Outcomes depend on individual facts and are not a guarantee of results. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions What does the Bihar Startup Policy actually give? A seed grant of up to ₹10 lakh per startup as an interest-free loan for 10 years at the validation stage (higher for women- and SC/ST-led startups), a ₹3 lakh grant on completing an approved accelerator programme, and further post-seed support for startups that cross early revenue milestones. Plus free co-working space, patent-filing support and reservation of 10% of space in new industrial parks for startups. Who is eligible? An entity incorporated or registered in Bihar with a functioning office in Bihar, within the policy's age and turnover limits, whose taxes are payable in Bihar, recognised as a startup by the Nodal Agency (Department of Industries) through startup.bihar.gov.in. Recognition precedes funding; they are separate steps. How does the money come? As a loan, not a grant, despite the name — interest-free, repayable over 10 years, released against milestones after a rating by the Startup Support Unit. It is non-dilutive: no equity is taken. Is this the same as Startup India / DPIIT recognition? No. DPIIT recognition is central (turnover limit now ₹200 crore) and unlocks tax and procurement benefits; Bihar recognition is state-level and unlocks the state seed fund and space. Most Bihar startups should hold both, and the applications share documents. Can an NCR founder apply by registering a Bihar entity? Only if the business is genuinely incorporated and operating from Bihar — office, operations and tax base in the state. A Patna address on paper with the team in Noida does not qualify and is exactly what the screening looks for. What is the Bihar Startup Scale-up Financing Fund? A ₹50 crore fund-of-funds managed by SIDBI that invests through SEBI-registered AIFs rather than directly — relevant once a startup is raising institutional money, not at seed stage. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Trademark in Noida — registry, classes, timeline Item For Noida applicants Registry of jurisdiction Trade Marks Registry, Delhi (jurisdiction for Uttar Pradesh) Hearings (objection / opposition) Delhi Government fee per class ₹4,500 (individual / startup / Udyam MSME, e-filing) · ₹9,000 (others) Validity 10 years from filing, renewable Typical Noida class mix SaaS, IT services and electronics brands — Class 9 (software, devices), Class 42 (software services), Class 35 (online retail) — plus Sector 18 restaurant and café brands in Class 43 What is specific to Noida: Noida brands usually need a Class 9 + Class 42 pair, and founders routinely file only one. The second most common error is a name already taken as a company name on MCA but clear on the registry — or the reverse — so we search both before filing. What we do Clearance search across word, phonetic, device and transliterated variants — and the MCA company-name register, so you don't clear one and collide with the other Class selection and specification drafting that matches what you actually sell Filing (TM-A) with the right applicant category for the ₹4,500 fee where you qualify Examination-report replies (Section 9 / 11), show-cause hearings, and opposition or counter-statement proceedings — in person at Delhi where required Post-registration: renewal, assignment, licensing, watch service, and infringement notices Copyright for logos and content, and design registration for product shapes, where they add protection the trademark alone doesn't Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Client: A Sector 62 SaaS startup with a one-word brand. Situation: Filed in Class 42 only; an objection cited a Class 9 mark with a similar prefix, and the examination report was two weeks from deadline. Approach: Drafted the response distinguishing goods, trade channels and consumers, added the Class 9 application defensively, and attended the show-cause hearing. Outcome: Objection waived; mark advertised and registered in both classes. Client identity and certain details have been changed or withheld to protect confidentiality. Outcomes depend on individual facts and are not a guarantee of results. Related: company registration in Noida (file the mark in the company's name from day one) and the Noida GST practice . Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which Trade Marks Registry handles applications from Noida? The Trade Marks Registry, Delhi (jurisdiction for Uttar Pradesh), decided by the applicant's principal place of business. Filing is online nationally, but examination, objections and hearings sit with that office — hearings for Noida applicants are in Delhi. Which classes do Noida businesses usually need? It depends on the goods or services, but the typical Noida profile is SaaS, IT services and electronics brands — Class 9 (software, devices), Class 42 (software services), Class 35 (online retail) — plus Sector 18 restaurant and café brands in Class 43. Filing in the wrong or an incomplete set of classes is the most expensive mistake — a new application is needed to add a class later. What does trademark registration cost? Government fee ₹4,500 per class for individuals, startups and Udyam-registered MSMEs filing online, ₹9,000 per class for others. A registration lasts 10 years and is renewable indefinitely. Our professional fee is quoted after the search, before filing. How long does it take? Filing to examination report typically runs a few months; if no objection or opposition arises, registration commonly follows within 12 to 18 months of filing. You can use the ™ symbol from filing and ® only after registration. What happens if I get an objection? An examination report under Section 9 (descriptiveness) or Section 11 (similarity) must be answered within 30 days; a hearing may follow. Most objections are answerable with a properly argued reply and evidence — abandonment usually comes from missing the deadline, not from the merits. Can I file before incorporating my company? Yes — an individual or proprietor can apply, and the mark can be assigned to the company later. If incorporation is imminent, filing in the company's name avoids an assignment step; we sequence it with the incorporation. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Jurisdiction is PAN-based: your Assessing Officer sits in the Noida charge of the Income Tax Department (Uttar Pradesh region) for most Noida addresses, while filing itself is on the national e-filing portal. Notices and hearings come from that local office — we appear there. What kind of tax work is typical in Noida? Salaried IT professionals with ESOPs/RSUs and foreign stock, consultants on presumptive 44ADA, and Sector 62–63 companies running monthly TDS on salaries, contractors and rent. What changed with the Income-tax Act, 2025? It took effect on 1 April 2026. 'Tax Year' replaces the old Previous Year / Assessment Year, and forms and section numbers are being renumbered under the Income-tax Rules, 2026 (the tax audit report, for instance, is now Form 26). Income for FY 2025-26 is still governed by the 1961 Act. We file under whichever applies to the year in question. When are returns due? For individuals and non-audit cases the standard date is 31 July; non-audit ITR-3/ITR-4 filers have 31 August for AY 2026-27; audit cases 31 October. An updated return (ITR-U) can be filed within 48 months where income was under-reported. Dates are per the Board's notifications and we track extensions. Old or new regime? Under the new regime, income up to ₹12 lakh carries no tax (₹12.75 lakh for salaried with standard deduction). Whether the old regime still wins depends on your deductions — HRA, home-loan interest, 80C/80D. We compute both before filing, not by default. I got an income tax notice — what now? Read the section first: 143(1) is an intimation, 139(9) a defective return, 142(1)/143(2) scrutiny, 148 reassessment. Each has a different deadline and reply route on the e-filing portal. ## https://udyoggrowth.com/pollution-noc-noida-ghaziabad/
Pollution NOC Noida & Ghaziabad — CTE/CTO Consultant Udyog Growth ☰ Subsidies & Finance PMFME & MoFPI Subsidy MSME Schemes Business Loans & Subsidy CMA Data & Bankable DPR GST, Tenders & Trade Regulatory Affairs Labour Code / EPF / ESIC BIS Certification ISO Certification PESO License Industrial Approvals Advance Authorisation / EPCG GeM Suspension / Disputes CMA Data / DPR GST Notices & Litigation GeM & Tenders Import-Export (IEC/DGFT) Advance Authorisation & EPCG GeM Suspension & Disputes Licensing & Approvals FSSAI Food License Liquor & Excise (Delhi) Land Conversion / CLU Solar Subsidy Pollution NOC PESO License Industrial Approvals & SEZ Labour & Certification Labour Code, EPF & ESIC BIS Certification (ISI/CRS) ISO Certification NGO & Schools NGO / Trust / CSR School Affiliation (CBSE/CISCE) Delhi Nursery Admissions Delhi Top Schools List Regulatory Affairs Cities Delhi & New Delhi Noida & Greater Noida Gurugram Faridabad Ghaziabad Patna Bihar (all districts) BIADA & Bihar incentives Tools All services Call Home / Pollution NOC Noida & Ghaziabad Pollution NOC Noida & Ghaziabad — CTE & CTO Quick answer: Units in Noida & Ghaziabad take Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate from the Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB) (not DPCC). Category under the 2025 CPCB schedule decides whether you need a full consent or only an intimation, what controls you install and how long consent lasts. We classify first, prepare the technical file, and handle the inspection. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. CTE and CTO in Noida & Ghaziabad — the board, the portal, the timeline Item Noida & Ghaziabad Authority Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB) Portal UPPCB's online consent system (OCMMS), also routed through Nivesh Mitra 3.0 Offices Regional offices for Gautam Buddh Nagar and Ghaziabad Consent to Establish (CTE) Before construction or installation; one-time per establishment or expansion Consent to Operate (CTO) Before production; renewable, term depends on category Categories Red / Orange / Green / White (CPCB pollution index; 2025 schedule) Alongside Hazardous-waste authorisation, bio-medical waste (clinics), CGWA groundwater NOC for borewells, fire NOC, ETP/STP design What is specific here: UPPCB consent runs through its OCMMS portal and, for new units, through the Nivesh Mitra single window — two logins, one file. Approval commonly takes 60–90 days after inspection; consents are issued for multi-year terms by category (longer for green). UP also requires a separate authorisation for hazardous waste and, for many Noida units, a CGWA/UP groundwater NOC for borewells that UPPCB inspectors ask about on site. We serve units across Noida Phase 1–3 and Sectors 57–65, Sector 80–81 and Hosiery Complex, NSEZ, Greater Noida's Ecotech sectors and Kasna/Surajpur industrial areas, and Ghaziabad's Sahibabad Site 4, Meerut Road, Bulandshahr Road, Kavi Nagar and Loni belts. What we do Category classification first — against the 2025 CPCB schedule as adopted by the board — so you file the right application (or an intimation, if White) CTE application with site plan, process flow, water balance and pollution-control design; CTO with completion and monitoring records Technical annexures: ETP/STP sizing, stack specifications, hazardous-waste authorisation where applicable Inspection coordination at the regional office, and reply to any inspection observations or show-cause Renewals on a calendar, amendments for expansion or product change, and transfer on change of ownership Sequencing with factory licence , PESO (fuel storage), FSSAI and single-window approvals so inspections don't collide Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Client: A Sahibabad Site 4 printing and packaging unit expanding its line. Situation: Operating on an old CTO about to expire, with an expansion that changed its category from green to orange; a UPPCB inspection notice had already arrived. Approach: Filed the amended CTE for the expansion before the inspection, prepared the ETP and stack-monitoring records the orange category requires, and renewed the CTO on the new category in the same cycle. Outcome: Consent to Establish and renewed Consent to Operate issued on the correct category; no show-cause from the inspection. Client identity and certain details have been changed or withheld to protect confidentiality. Outcomes depend on individual facts and are not a guarantee of results. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which board issues pollution NOC in Noida & Ghaziabad? The Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board (UPPCB), through UPPCB's online consent system (OCMMS), also routed through Nivesh Mitra 3.0 — Regional offices for Gautam Buddh Nagar and Ghaziabad. Delhi units go to DPCC instead; the two systems, categories and fees are not interchangeable even for neighbouring premises. What is the difference between CTE and CTO? Consent to Establish is required before you build or install — it approves the plan, location and pollution-control design. Consent to Operate is required before you start production — it confirms the controls are built and working. CTO is renewed periodically; CTE is a one-time approval per establishment or expansion. What are red, orange, green and white categories? CPCB classifies industries by a Pollution Index. Red (60+) carries the heaviest conditions and shortest consent terms; orange (41–59) and green (21–40) progressively lighter; white (up to 20) is the lowest-impact set, now handled under a simplified intimation regime in states that have adopted the 2025 schedule rather than full consent. Your category decides fees, inspection, validity and whether you need an ETP. What documents are needed? Typically: proof of the entity and the site (lease/allotment), site plan and layout, process flow with raw materials and products, water balance and effluent/emission details, the pollution-control plan (ETP/STP/stack), capital investment figures (fees are investment-linked in most states), and for CTO the completion and monitoring reports. We prepare the technical annexures so the file is not returned. How long does pollution consent take? Portal service standards run from a few weeks for green to 60–90 days for orange and red after inspection; actual time depends on inspection scheduling and whether the file is complete. We track the file through the regional office rather than waiting on the portal status. Do I need consent for an office, warehouse or restaurant? Pure offices generally do not; warehouses, restaurants with DG sets, hotels and most workshops usually do, depending on state schedules and DG capacity. Many businesses either file unnecessarily or skip a required consent — we classify first. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which ROC handles a Delhi company? The Registrar of Companies, NCT of Delhi & Haryana (Nehru Place, New Delhi). Incorporation is filed centrally on MCA's SPICe+, but this ROC hears later filings, inspections and show-cause matters for Delhi companies. What is different about registering in Delhi versus Noida or Gurugram? Three things: Delhi stamp duty on MOA/AOA; Delhi's Shop & Establishment registration still applies at any headcount (the 2026 amendment raising it to 20 employees has been published but not yet brought into force), unlike UP and Haryana; and the trade/health trade licence comes from MCD or NDMC depending on the premises. No Professional Tax in Delhi. Do I need a commercial address in Delhi to register? You need a registered office with proof (ownership or NOC-plus-rent-agreement and a utility bill). A residential address is permitted for the registered office; a commercial activity at it may need MCD permission depending on the use — we check before you commit to the address. How long does it take? Name approval and SPICe+ filing are portal-driven; complete, correctly-documented applications are typically approved within MCA's standard window (around 7 working days as per portal SLA). Delays come from name conflicts, document defects or DSC problems. What comes with incorporation? Certificate of Incorporation with CIN, PAN, TAN, EPFO and ESIC registrations and a bank-account request through the single SPICe+/AGILE-PRO filing; GST optionally in the same filing. What compliance follows? INC-20A within 180 days, ADT-1, annual AOC-4 and MGT-7/7A, and DIR-3 KYC for each director — now once in three years from 31 March 2026. Under the revised small-company limits (₹10 crore capital / ₹100 crore turnover) most new companies get the lighter tier. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Anyone still quoting you 7–15 days as standard is not using it. We check eligibility, file to the rule, and set up the first cycle. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. Rule 14A vs the normal route Item Rule 14A (simplified) Normal route Who B2B output tax ≤ ₹2.5 lakh/month, Aadhaar-authenticated Everyone else, or applicants opting out Grant Electronically, within 3 working days After verification; physical verification possible Limit One Rule 14A registration per State/UT per PAN No such cap Exit Mandatory before output tax crosses ₹2.5 lakh/month — Legal basis CBIC Notification 18/2025–CT, 31 Oct 2025 (effective 1 Nov 2025) CGST Rules 8–9 Eligibility in one line: expected monthly output tax on supplies to registered buyers under ₹2.5 lakh, Aadhaar in hand, no existing Rule 14A GSTIN in the same state on your PAN — you qualify. Quick check: enter your expected monthly B2B sales; at 18% GST, ₹2.5 lakh of tax corresponds to roughly ₹13.9 lakh of B2B turnover per month. What we do Eligibility test and the right route — Rule 14A, normal, composition, or casual/non-resident where applicable Aadhaar authentication and a document set that matches PAN data exactly (the usual cause of queries) Principal and additional places of business, state-wise, with the correct jurisdictional officer Bank-account verification on the portal — unverified bank details suspend a new GSTIN and block GSTR-1/3B and e-way bills First-cycle setup: invoice series, HSN/SAC and GST 2.0 rates (5% / 18% / 40%), e-way bill and e-invoice thresholds, LUT for exporters Monitoring the ₹2.5 lakh threshold and handling the exit to regular registration before it bites Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Approach: Confirmed eligibility (projected B2B output tax well under ₹2.5 lakh/month), completed Aadhaar authentication, filed with documents aligned to PAN and lease, and verified the bank account on day one. City practices: Noida · Gurugram · Faridabad · Ghaziabad · Patna . Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions What is Rule 14A GST registration? A simplified registration route notified by CBIC (Notification 18/2025–Central Tax, 31 October 2025, effective 1 November 2025). Eligible applicants who complete Aadhaar authentication are granted registration electronically within three working days, instead of the standard verification track. Who is eligible for the 3-working-day route? Applicants whose output tax on supplies to registered persons (B2B) will not exceed ₹2.5 lakh per month — CGST, SGST/UTGST and IGST combined — and who complete Aadhaar authentication. Only one Rule 14A registration is allowed per State or Union Territory per PAN. Higher-risk or above-threshold applicants follow the normal route with physical verification where required. What if my B2B output tax later crosses ₹2.5 lakh a month? You must exit the simplified route and move to a regular registration through the prescribed process before crossing the limit; continuing on Rule 14A above the threshold invites proceedings. We track the figure monthly for clients on this route. Is the 3-day timeline guaranteed? It is the rule's service standard for complete, Aadhaar-authenticated, eligible applications. An incomplete application, a mismatch between PAN data and documents, or a flagged address still triggers a query — which is what we prevent before filing. Does Rule 14A apply in Delhi, UP, Haryana and Bihar alike? Yes — it is a CGST rule mirrored in every State GST law. What differs by state is the jurisdictional officer who handles any query: CGST Delhi Zone / Delhi Trade & Taxes, UP State Tax (Noida, Ghaziabad), Haryana Excise & Taxation (Gurugram, Faridabad), Bihar Commercial Taxes (Patna). I was quoted 7 to 15 days for GST registration — is that still right? For eligible applicants, no. The 3-working-day Rule 14A track exists precisely to replace that. If a vendor is quoting two weeks as standard, they are either not using the route or you fall outside its conditions — we tell you which before you pay anyone. © 2026 Udyog Growth. What is Bihar's ODOP under PMFME? One District One Product assigns each Bihar district a focus food product — makhana in the Mithila belt (Darbhanga, Madhubani), litchi in Muzaffarpur, banana in Vaishali, maize in Khagaria, Katarni rice, honey, sattu and mango among others. The official district list is on the State Nodal Agency's portal — we match your product to it before filing. How much is the subsidy and how does it reach me? 35% of eligible project cost as a credit-linked capital subsidy, capped at ₹10 lakh per unit, routed through the bank loan: the bank sanctions, the subsidy is credited and held, and is adjusted after three years of the unit operating. There is also seed capital of ₹40,000 per SHG member for working capital and small tools, and 35% up to ₹3 crore for common infrastructure of FPOs, SHGs and cooperatives. Who is the DRP and do I need one? District Resource Persons are empanelled by the State Nodal Agency to help applicants with DPRs and bank liaison; using one is optional. We work alongside the DRP where the applicant has one and replace that function where they don't — the difference is that we also run the FSSAI, pollution, Udyam and GST files the bank asks about. Which banks in Bihar sanction PMFME loans? Public-sector banks, regional rural banks and cooperative banks all participate; sanction depends on the branch's view of the DPR and the applicant's profile. We prepare the DPR to what credit committees in Bihar actually test — realistic capacity utilisation, raw-material sourcing from the district, and a working-capital cycle that matches the product's season. Can an NCR business set up a PMFME unit in Bihar? Yes, if the unit is physically in Bihar and the applicant meets the scheme's eligibility (individual/proprietor, partnership, FPO, SHG, cooperative, or company for certain categories). The five registrations a Patna employer actually needs Registration Applies at Authority Note Shop & Establishment (Bihar) Shops and commercial establishments in notified areas Labour Resources Department, Bihar (online portal) No 20-employee threshold in Bihar (unlike UP/Haryana) Professional Tax Employers and employees above the slab Commercial Taxes Department, Bihar Levied in Bihar; not in Delhi-NCR — deductible for income tax ESIC 10+ employees ESIC Regional Office, Bihar (Patna) Wage ceiling ₹21,000; register employees within 10 days of joining EPF 20+ employees EPFO Regional Office, Patna (Bhavishyanidhi Bhawan, R-Block) Wage ceiling ₹15,000 for mandatory coverage; ECR by the 15th Factory licence (manufacturers) 20+ workers with power / 40+ without Labour Resources Department under the OSH Code Plan approval is a physical step; BIADA units need it before CTO Bihar-specific, current as of 4 October 2026: Bihar has not raised its Shop Act threshold, and it levies Professional Tax — two things that make a Patna payroll file different from a Noida or Gurugram one. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Does my Patna office need Shop & Establishment registration? Yes — Bihar's Shops and Establishments Act applies to shops and commercial establishments in notified areas, and Bihar has not adopted the 20-employee threshold that UP and Haryana introduced in 2025. Registration is through the Bihar Labour Resources Department's online portal; we file it with the registers the inspector checks. Does Bihar have Professional Tax? Yes. Unlike Delhi, UP and Haryana, Bihar levies Professional Tax on employers and employees under the Bihar Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 2011, administered by the Commercial Taxes Department. A Patna employer needs the PT registration (and enrolment) alongside Shop Act, EPF and ESIC — most NCR-based advice misses it. When do EPF and ESIC apply in Patna? EPF at 20 or more employees (wage ceiling ₹15,000 for mandatory coverage; 12% + 12%); ESIC at 10 or more employees in notified areas (wage ceiling ₹21,000; 0.75% + 3.25%). The ₹30,000 ESIC ceiling you may have read about has not been notified. Patna is a notified ESIC area. Which offices handle it? EPFO Regional Office, Patna (Bhavishyanidhi Bhawan, R-Block) for PF establishments; ESIC Regional Office, Bihar, in Patna; the Labour Resources Department for Shop Act and the OSH Code registrations; the Commercial Taxes Department for Professional Tax. We appear at all four — verify current addresses on the respective portals before visiting. What changed with the Labour Codes for a Bihar employer? The four Codes took effect on 21 November 2025. For a Patna establishment the practical items are the wage definition (basic + DA at least 50% of total pay), mandatory appointment letters, single registration under the OSH Code at 10+ workers, and the factory-licence threshold at 20+ workers with power. Bihar's state rules are being notified; we check the live status before filing. Can you handle a PMFME or BIADA unit's labour registrations too? Yes — most Bihar food-processing units we set up need Shop Act or factory licence, EPF, ESIC and Professional Tax sequenced with the FSSAI licence, BSPCB consent and the bank file. Most Delhi-NCR detentions are procedural — an expired bill in traffic, a Part B error — and the minor-discrepancy circulars and the intent test decide them. We respond the same day. Detention to release — the timeline that matters Stage Form Your window What we do Interception & statement MOV-01 / MOV-02 Immediate Advise the driver what to sign and what not to; get documents to the officer Physical verification MOV-04 Same day Ensure the report records quantity and documents accurately Detention order & notice MOV-06 / MOV-07 7 days to reply Reply on facts: transport record, toll/FASTag data, invoice, payment of tax, the minor-discrepancy circulars Release Payment or MOV-08 bond + security Before the order where goods are perishable Secure release while preserving the right to contest Penalty order MOV-09 Appeal within 3 months, 25% pre-deposit APL-01 with the full evidence set Confiscation (if unpaid) MOV-10 / MOV-11 Reply to MOV-10 Prevent escalation; section 130 requires intent The argument that wins most NCR cases: section 129 is attracted by contravention, but section 130 and the heavier outcomes require intent to evade. Tax paid, invoice matching, goods matching, bill expired by hours in traffic — that is a procedural lapse, and the record (FASTag timestamps, transporter's GPS, the invoice-and-payment trail) has to be assembled fast enough to say so within seven days. Outcomes depend on individual facts and are not a guarantee of results. Part of our GST notice-defence practice . City pages: Ghaziabad · Noida · Gurugram · Faridabad . Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Goods detained on the road — what is the sequence of forms? MOV-01 (driver's statement) → MOV-02 (order for physical verification) → MOV-04 (verification report) → MOV-06 (detention order) → MOV-07 (notice proposing penalty under section 129) → MOV-09 (penalty order). If penalty is not paid, MOV-10/MOV-11 start confiscation under section 130. Your reply window is the MOV-07 stage — seven days — and that is where the case is won or lost. How much is the penalty under section 129? Where the owner comes forward: 200% of the tax payable on taxable goods (2% of value or ₹25,000, whichever is less, for exempt goods). Where the owner does not come forward: the higher of 50% of the value of goods or 200% of tax. Goods and the vehicle are released on payment, or on a bond with security of equal amount (MOV-08) while you contest. The e-way bill had a small error — is the full penalty still payable? Not necessarily. CBIC's circulars on minor discrepancies (spelling errors, a wrong pin code within the same place, a vehicle-number digit, a document-number error) direct a token penalty under section 125 (₹500 CGST + ₹500 SGST) instead of section 129. An expired e-way bill where the goods are genuinely in transit with tax paid is routinely contested on the 'no intent to evade' ground — the courts have repeatedly accepted it when the record shows it. Can I appeal the penalty order? Yes — to the Appellate Authority under section 107 within three months, with a pre-deposit of 25% of the penalty for section 129 orders. If the goods are perishable or the vehicle is a business asset, we usually secure release on bond first and then appeal. Why does this happen so often at the Delhi border? Daily dispatches between Delhi and Ghaziabad, Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad cross a state line, so every consignment needs an inter-state e-way bill and Part B with the vehicle; traffic delays expire bills on short-haul trips, and mobile squads on NH-9, NH-48 and the Noida and Faridabad entry points check them. Most detentions we handle are procedural lapses, not evasion. Do you appear before the mobile squad and the adjudicating officer? Yes — the MOV-07 reply, the hearing, release on payment or bond, and the appeal. In Delhi-NCR the proper officer is usually the State mobile squad of the state where the goods were intercepted (UP, Haryana or Delhi), not your home jurisdiction. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Notice types — deadline and route Notice What it is Deadline Route 143(1) Intimation after processing; may carry a demand or refund 30 days if you disagree Rectification u/s 154 or response to adjustment 139(9) Defective return 15 days Revised/corrected return on the portal 142(1) Inquiry — documents, or a return if not filed As stated e-Proceedings reply with documents 143(2) Scrutiny Served within 3 months of the FY end in which the return was filed Faceless assessment; replies, video hearing on request 148A / 148 Show-cause, then reassessment As stated (minimum 7 days for 148A) Reply to 148A first; return in response to 148 156 Demand 30 days Pay, or stay application with appeal 245 Refund adjusted against old demand Respond within the window Agree/disagree with reasons 270A / 271AAC etc. Penalty As stated Reply; immunity under 270AA where available What actually triggers most notices now: AIS/TIS mismatches (interest, dividends, share and property transactions you didn't report), high-value cash or UPI inflows, TDS credit claimed that isn't in 26AS, foreign assets missing from Schedule FA, and old-regime deductions claimed without proof. The reply has to reconcile the department's data to your return line by line — not argue in general. Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which income tax notice have I got, and how long do I have? Read the section on the first page. 143(1) is a processing intimation — act within 30 days if you disagree. 139(9) is a defective return — 15 days to fix it. 142(1) asks for information or a return. 143(2) opens scrutiny. 148A is the show-cause before reassessment; 148 is the reassessment notice itself. 156 is a demand — pay or respond within 30 days. 245 adjusts a refund against an old demand. Every one has a different route on the e-filing portal. I got a 143(1) with a demand — is it final? No. It is an automated adjustment (arithmetical errors, mismatches with Form 26AS/AIS, disallowed claims). If it is wrong, file a rectification under section 154 or respond to the proposed adjustment; if it is right, pay before interest grows. Most 143(1) demands we see come from TDS not reflected in 26AS or a wrong regime selection. Can the department reopen my old returns? Reassessment under section 148 is subject to time limits — three years from the end of the relevant assessment year in the normal case, extended where escaped income represented by an asset or expenditure is ₹50 lakh or more — and must be preceded by a 148A show-cause notice giving you a chance to respond. The 148A reply is where reassessment is often stopped. Everything is faceless now — do I still need someone to appear? Assessment is faceless (e-Proceedings), but the reply quality, the documents and the request for a video hearing decide outcomes, and appeals before CIT(A) and ITAT still need representation. We draft, upload and attend. What changed under the Income-tax Act, 2025? From 1 April 2026 the new Act applies with 'Tax Year' terminology and renumbered sections; notices for earlier years continue under the 1961 Act. A reply must cite the correct Act and section for the year in question — mixing them is a common error in templated replies. What if I ignore the notice? Best-judgment assessment under 144, penalties (270A for under-reporting, 272A for non-compliance), interest, and in reassessment cases the loss of the chance to explain before the notice. Even a request for more time is better than silence. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Section 9 is won on distinctiveness and evidence of use; Section 11 on a mark-by-mark comparison of the cited marks. We draft the reply with annexures and appear at the hearing — Delhi registry for NCR, Kolkata for Bihar. Last verified 4 October 2026 — rules on this page checked against the current notifications. We update it the day a rule changes. The objection timeline — and the two deadlines that abandon applications Stage Deadline Consequence of missing it Examination report (Sec. 9 / 11 objection) 30 days to file reply Application deemed abandoned Show-cause hearing As listed; adjournments limited Refusal on non-appearance Advertisement in TM Journal Opposition window: 4 months — Notice of opposition received 2 months to file counter-statement (TM-O) Application deemed abandoned Evidence rounds & hearing Per Rules 45–50 Decision on merits What a winning Section 9 reply contains: an argument that the mark is suggestive rather than descriptive; dictionary and trade evidence; and, where the mark has been in use, a user affidavit with sales figures, invoices, advertising spend and media coverage to claim acquired distinctiveness. What a winning Section 11 reply contains: a mark-by-mark comparison of each cited mark — goods, class, trade channel, consumer, visual and phonetic impression — plus status checks (many cited marks are abandoned or unrenewed) and consent letters where a coexistence agreement is possible. What we do Read the examination report the day it issues and calendar the 30 days Draft the reply with evidence annexures — user affidavit, invoices, search reports on cited marks Appear at the show-cause hearing (Delhi or Kolkata registry; video where listed) Opposition: counter-statement within two months, evidence by affidavit, hearing Review and appeal of refusals; rectification against conflicting registrations where that is the cleaner route Parallel strategy: a composite or amended mark filed defensively while the original is argued Illustrative client engagement — details anonymised. Client: A Sector 62 SaaS startup with a one-word brand. Situation: Section 11 objection citing a Class 9 mark with a similar prefix; two weeks left on the 30-day clock. Approach: Mark-by-mark comparison on goods, channel and consumer; evidence of the cited mark's narrow specification; defensive Class 9 filing; appearance at the hearing. Outcome: Objection waived; mark advertised and registered. Client identity and certain details have been changed or withheld to protect confidentiality. Outcomes depend on individual facts and are not a guarantee of results. Filing a new mark? City pages: Noida · Gurugram · Faridabad · Patna . Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions What is a trademark objection? An examination report from the Trade Marks Registry raising objections under Section 9 (absolute grounds — the mark is descriptive, generic or non-distinctive) and/or Section 11 (relative grounds — it conflicts with earlier marks). It is not a refusal; it is a chance to argue. You must file a reply within 30 days of receiving the report or the application is treated as abandoned. Section 9 vs Section 11 — what is the difference in the reply? Section 9 is argued on distinctiveness: the mark is suggestive not descriptive, or has acquired distinctiveness through use (user affidavit, sales, advertising, media). Section 11 is argued on dissimilarity: the cited marks differ in goods, trade channels, consumers, or visually/phonetically — or they are dead, unrenewed or the owner consents. Each cited mark needs its own answer. What happens after the reply? The examiner either accepts the mark (it is advertised in the Trade Marks Journal) or lists a show-cause hearing. At the hearing we appear with evidence; acceptance, conditional acceptance or refusal follows. Refusal can be reviewed and appealed. What is an opposition and how is it different? After advertisement, any person can oppose within four months. You then have two months from receipt of the notice of opposition to file a counter-statement, failing which the application is abandoned. Evidence rounds follow, then a hearing. Oppositions from established brands are common in crowded classes. Can I keep using the mark while the objection is pending? Yes — with ™, not ®. Using the mark and documenting that use actually strengthens an acquired-distinctiveness argument under Section 9. Which registry hears my case? Delhi for Delhi, Haryana and UP applicants (Noida, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad); Kolkata for Bihar (Patna). Hearings are increasingly by video, but the examiner practice and listing speed differ by office. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Since 1 November 2025 low-risk claims get 90% provisionally through the system — if the first filing is complete. We reconcile invoice by invoice before filing, renew the LUT every April, and track FEMA realisation so a refund never turns into a recovery. Which refund route — and what each needs Situation Route Key document Typical trap Export of goods/services without IGST LUT (RFD-11) + refund of unutilised ITC via RFD-01 Statement 3 with invoices and BRC/FIRC LUT not renewed in April; ITC on capital goods wrongly included Export with payment of IGST Refund through shipping bill / GSTR-1 Table 6A Shipping bill, EGM, matched GSTR-3B Invoice value mismatch between GSTR-1 and shipping bill blocks the claim Supplies to SEZ LUT or IGST-paid, refund by supplier SEZ officer endorsement Missing endorsement Inverted duty structure Refund of accumulated ITC (formula-based) Statement 1A Input services excluded from the formula; wrong net ITC Deemed exports (EOU, Advance Authorisation supplies) Refund by supplier or recipient Recipient's undertaking Both parties claiming Excess cash-ledger balance / wrong head RFD-01 (excess balance) Ledger extract Filing under the wrong category What changed: system-based provisional refunds of 90% for low-risk zero-rated and inverted-duty claims apply from 1 November 2025, cutting the wait from months to days for clean files — which makes a complete first filing worth more than ever, because a deficiency memo drops you out of the fast track. GST 2.0's rate changes (22 September 2025) also moved several products out of, or into, an inverted position; we re-test the formula for every client. Exporters in Gurugram , Noida , Faridabad and Delhi . Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions LUT or pay IGST and claim refund — which is better for an exporter? Under a Letter of Undertaking (RFD-11) you export without charging IGST and claim refund of the unutilised input tax credit; with payment of IGST you pay on the export invoice and the refund flows through the shipping bill once GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B match. LUT keeps cash in the business; the IGST route is simpler to reconcile where ITC is small. Most NCR service exporters use LUT; many goods exporters run both depending on the ITC position. When do I file the LUT? Before the first export of the financial year — it is valid for that year only. File it every April; an export made without a live LUT means IGST was due on that invoice, which is a common audit finding in Cyber City and Noida IT firms. What is the time limit for a refund claim? Two years from the relevant date — for exports of goods, the date the vessel/aircraft leaves or the goods cross the border; for services, the date of receipt of convertible foreign exchange (or the invoice date, whichever is later); for unutilised ITC, the end of the financial year in which the claim arises. Claims are filed in RFD-01 on the portal with the statement for the category. How fast does the refund come? Acknowledgement (RFD-02) or deficiency memo (RFD-03) within 15 days of filing; for zero-rated supplies and inverted-duty claims, system-based provisional sanction of 90% for low-risk claims has applied since 1 November 2025, with the balance after scrutiny; the final order is due within 60 days, after which interest at 6% runs. A deficiency memo restarts the clock — so the first filing must be complete. I exported under LUT but the foreign payment is late — what happens? Export proceeds must be realised within the FEMA timeline (ordinarily nine months). If they aren't, the IGST that was waived becomes payable with interest, and the refund already taken can be recovered. We track BRC/FIRC status against each shipping bill or invoice. Which office processes my refund? Your jurisdictional officer — Centre or State as assigned to your GSTIN — not the customs port. In Delhi-NCR that means CGST Delhi/Haryana/Ghaziabad or the respective State Tax office; IGST-paid export refunds are processed through ICEGATE against the shipping bill. © 2026 Udyog Growth. Each cloud-kitchen premises needs its own licence; the platform's does not cover you. This page maps every business type to its licence and what the inspector checks. Licence type by business type — 2026 tiers Business type Licence Decided by Watch for Home kitchen, tiffin, petty seller, hawker Basic Registration (Form A) Turnover ≤ ₹1.5 crore Premises = home address; platforms need the number Cloud kitchen / virtual brands Basic or State per kitchen premises Turnover; each premises separately Platform's Central licence does not cover you; list every brand's products Restaurant, café, bakery retail, caterer Basic ≤ ₹1.5 cr · State ≤ ₹50 cr · Central above Turnover 4-star+ hotels: higher State fee; bars: excise after FSSAI Manufacturer / processor State or Central Turnover, or capacity (> 2 MT/day; dairy > 50,000 L/day → Central) Capacity declaration; layout plan; water test Trader, wholesaler, distributor, storage Basic / State / Central by turnover Turnover; cold storage capacity thresholds Multiple godowns = multiple licences Importer / exporter Central Activity Port clearance; labelling compliance E-commerce food operator / marketplace Central Activity Sellers on the platform need their own Head office of multi-state units Central (HO) + licence per unit Structure HO licence does not replace unit licences Railways, airports, seaports, Central Govt premises Central Location Regardless of turnover Tiers in force since 1 April 2026: Basic ≤ ₹1.5 crore · State ₹1.5–50 crore · Central above ₹50 crore (or by activity above). Talk to us before you file anything Call for a free consultation Frequently asked questions Which FSSAI licence does a cloud kitchen need? By turnover like any food business — Basic up to ₹1.5 crore, State to ₹50 crore — filed as a manufacturer/caterer at each kitchen premises; every physical kitchen needs its own registration or licence, and virtual brands running from one kitchen sit under that premises' licence with the products listed. The delivery platform's Central e-commerce licence does not cover your kitchen. Does a home kitchen or tiffin service need FSSAI? Yes — Basic Registration (Form A, ₹100 a year) up to ₹1.5 crore turnover, with the home address as the premises. Petty manufacturers and hawkers register too. Platforms and corporate clients ask for the number before onboarding. Restaurant, café, bar — State or Central? Turnover decides: Basic to ₹1.5 crore, State to ₹50 crore, Central above. A 4-star-plus hotel pays the higher State fee band. A bar needs the excise licence sequenced after FSSAI — the excise file asks for the FSSAI number. When does a manufacturer need a Central licence regardless of turnover? Capacity: above 2 MT per day (solids), dairy above 50,000 litres a day, large slaughterhouses and meat processors, and any unit in Central Government premises, railways, airports or seaports. Below those, turnover decides. Do importers, exporters and e-commerce operators need Central? Yes — importers and exporters by activity, e-commerce food operators and marketplaces by activity, and a head office of units in more than one state. These are Central regardless of turnover, and importers also deal with FSSAI's import-clearance system at the port. What does every category need besides the licence? A FoSTaC-trained food safety supervisor (one per 25 handlers), medical fitness certificates for handlers, a water-test report, pest-control records, the annual fee under perpetual validity, and the annual return (Form D1) for manufacturers and larger FBOs. Hygiene rating is voluntary but now expected by platforms and institutional buyers. © 2026 Udyog Growth.
